title: Federated Learning & Privacy-Preserving ML
tagline: Train models without collecting the data: federated averaging, Flower simulations, differential privacy, secure aggregation, encryption, and the attacks these defend against.
prereqs: Deep Learning (PyTorch training loops). Basic probability from Python & Math for AI helps for the differential privacy steps.

steps.title: What is federated learning?
steps.why: Train on many devices and share model updates instead of raw data.

steps.title: Federated learning in production
steps.why: How Google trains phone keyboard models across millions of devices.

steps.title: Federated learning algorithms
steps.why: University lecture on FedAvg and the algorithms built on it.

steps.title: Your first Flower simulation
steps.why: Simulate federated training of a PyTorch model with Flower.

steps.title: Stateful clients in Flower
steps.why: Keep per-client state across rounds, as personalized methods need.

steps.title: Differential privacy
steps.why: Add calibrated noise so no single person changes the result much.

steps.title: The definition of differential privacy
steps.why: Cynthia Dwork, who co-invented it, explains the formal definition.

steps.title: Differential privacy in deep learning
steps.why: Whether DP stops models memorizing data, and tips for using it.

steps.title: Membership inference attacks
steps.why: How attackers tell whether a record was in the training set.

steps.title: Secure aggregation
steps.why: The server learns the sum of client updates, not each update.

steps.title: Homomorphic encryption
steps.why: Compute on encrypted data without decrypting it first.

steps.title: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs
steps.why: A benchmark for fine-tuning language models across many data owners.

projects: Simulate 10 Flower clients on CIFAR-10, split the data so each client sees only two classes, and compare accuracy with centralized training.
Train an MNIST model with and without DP-SGD using Opacus and plot accuracy against the privacy budget epsilon.
Run a simple loss-threshold membership inference attack on an overfit model and on a regularized one, and compare how often it succeeds.
